key_insight: Population gradient flow can predict recovery after pretraining, but finite-batch SGD can fail to recover because rare ReLU gate disagreements drive the critical updates.
engineering_relevance: For training and fine-tuning deployed neural models, the result shows that batch size, step size, and pretraining duration can interact to create hard-to-see plasticity loss that gradient-flow analyses may miss.
method: Two-unit ReLU regression with a source task that aligns neurons and a target task that benefits from separating them.
Compare population gradient flow against exact online SGD with finite batch size and step size across pretraining and target phases.
Analyze gate-disagreement probability and track its cumulative occurrence along the discrete SGD recursion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that failure occurs with high probability over a horizon of about e^{c/η} once T is large enough, and that recovery requires Nb  e^{bbT} plus b  ηe^{bbT} in the target phase.
watch_item: The main mechanism depends on rare disagreement events and long-pretraining/small-step regimes, so conclusions may be most relevant when batch size is too small to reliably sample the critical wedge.
paper_title: Rare Gate Disagreements Can Limit Plasticity: When Gradient Flow Mispredicts Finite-Batch SGD
